sg.ra: These are the top-priced Center Orchestra seats.
The furthest side seats are farther from the opposite side of the stage. Avoid double-digit Right Orchestra seats if a partial view of the right-hand stage corner is a concern.
The overhang begins at row M and can cut off the top of the stage from seats behind it. Rear Orchestra is a value-for-money choice.

sn.c: At the far ends of the Left and Right Orchestra and in the back corners, views turn side-on and more restricted.
sn.sh: Far side and corner seats see the stage side-on

sn.c: The far side seats of the Mezzanine are the ones to avoid, at least on a first visit.
sn.sh: Far side Mezzanine seats are best avoided

sn.lo: Center Mezzanine, rows H to K
sn.c: Center Mezzanine rows H to K are good value, and the section's strong rake keeps the view clear from any seat.
sn.sh: Good value with a clear raked view

sn.lo: Center Mezzanine, rows L to M
sn.c: The back rows of the Center Mezzanine, L and M, are the cheapest seats in the theater. They feel distant but are a solid pick on a budget.
sn.sh: Cheapest seats in the house, but distant

sn.c: The Mezzanine overhang begins over Orchestra row M and can clip the top of the stage for seats behind it, though it rarely gets in the way.
Row A of the Center Mezzanine has clear, unblocked elevated sightlines, and some people prefer it to any Orchestra seat.

vs.sum: The Marquis Theatre offers excellent comfort with spacious seating and good sightlines from most areas, although the ambiance is somewhat lacking due to its modern, hotel-integrated design. Facilities are well-equipped with ample restrooms and concessions, making it a convenient choice for theatergoers.

acc.note: Elevator via Marriott Marquis hotel. 10 wheelchair spaces. No elevator to Mezzanine.
